chunks.title: CLO 2026.0 - 2D
chunks.content: # CLO 2026.0 - 2D Tools and Features This document covers the 2D measurement and calculation tools in CLO 2026.0, focusing on the **Measurement Point Computer**, **Computer Department**, **EPA tool**, **Hook tool**, **Checkbox editor improvements**, and the **T-shape expansion function**. It explains how to perform precise garment measurements, manage calculation formulas, and optimize 2D workspace efficiency. --- ## Measurement Point Computer and Computer Department Overview This section explains the **Measurement Point Computer**, a dynamic interface for creating mathematical formulas linked directly to clothing measurement points, and the **Computer Department**, which manages and stores these calculation results. ### Measurement Point Computer - The **Measurement Point Computer** allows direct mathematical calculations on 2D garment measurement points. - Formulas created link to 3D projects, eliminating the need for external spreadsheets. - It provides a dynamic interface for entering and applying formulas based on measurement points. ### Accessing the Measurement Point Computer There are four ways to open the Measurement Point Computer window: 1. Click the **Measurement Point Computer** icon. 2. Click the **Measurement Point** icon. 3. Access via the icon in the upper left corner of the screen. 4. Access via the icon in the upper right corner of the screen. All methods open an empty computer window ready for formula input. ### Using the Measurement Point Computer - Open the **cloud calculator** icon. - Select measurement points or self-defined measurement values and add them to the formula. - Use standard calculator operations; if input errors occur, press the **C** button to clear. - Use three different measurement points for calculations, then press **Return** or the **equal** button to finalize. - Click **Apply** to add the calculated result as a new measurement point in the computer. --- ## Computer Department: Managing Measurement Calculations This section details the **Computer Department**, a window for storing, managing, and displaying all formulas created with the Measurement Point Computer. ### Features and Navigation - Access via the **2D menu** on the top menu bar by selecting **Computer**. - Resize the window by dragging corners; minimize it with the arrow icon in the title bar to save screen space. - Default folder named **Default Folder** stores calculation results. - Create new folders with the **Add Folder** button. - Move calculations by right-clicking and selecting target folders. - Rename folders by double-clicking their names and pressing **Return** to confirm. - Delete folders using the trash can icon after selecting the folder. ### Updating and Applying Calculations - After adjusting measurement points or boards, click the **Update** button to refresh calculation data. - Click the measurement point icon next to a calculation to add it as a new measurement point. - The calculator icon next to added calculations allows their use in further formulas. - Delete calculations via the **Delete** icon; this does not remove the measurement point object itself. - The **Code** icon displays measurement values across code sizes such as M, L, XL.
chunks.content_description: CLO 2026.0 version is now officially released — Make it, for real! CLO technical experts present a detailed introduction to the "Measurement Point Calculator" and "Calculation Book" to optimize your 2D measurement workflow.

chunks.content: ### Updating and Applying Calculations - After adjusting measurement points or boards, click the **Update** button to refresh calculation data. - Click the measurement point icon next to a calculation to add it as a new measurement point. - The calculator icon next to added calculations allows their use in further formulas. - Delete calculations via the **Delete** icon; this does not remove the measurement point object itself. - The **Code** icon displays measurement values across code sizes such as M, L, XL. ### Importance Using these tools ensures **high-level technical accuracy** throughout the garment design process by maintaining consistent and manageable measurement formulas. --- ## EPA Tool Enhancements in CLO 2026.0 This section covers updates to the **EPA tool**, which improves fabric manipulation and adjustment processes in 2D. ### EPA (Ease Pull Adjustment) Tool Features - Updated scanning machine allows increasing the number of garment parts and provides enhanced scanning tool examination. - Grid structure of all panels is automatically displayed in the 2D window upon tool selection. - New animation settings enable selecting the correct size for each panel. - Scale size and hardness adjustable via an icon in the top right corner. ### Using EPA for Fabric Adjustments - To simulate pulling effects (e.g., front big body or front sleeve of a suit), set mode to **Increase** and scale to positive. - Enable simulation, then click and drag the target panel area; repeat if necessary. - To revert, keep the mode as **Increase** but set scale to negative. - Right-click on an EPA to delete individual or all EPAs, facilitating easy repetition of adjustments. ### Benefits - The EPA tool offers a more intuitive and accurate method for fabric fine-tuning, improving garment fit and fabric performance. --- ## Fabric Symmetry and Hook Outline Tool This section explains the **Hook Outline Tool** for managing symmetrical garment parts and updates to the **Hook function** for efficient editing in CLO 2026.0. ### Fabric Symmetry Checking - Use the **Hook Outline Tool** from the 2D toolbar. - Select symmetrical lines (inner, outer, or basic lines) by pressing **Shift** to select both sides simultaneously. - Right-click a selected line and choose **Hook as Board** to create a new board with active symmetrical links matching the original. - This eliminates extra steps after removing or opening hooks, keeping the workspace organized. ### Hook Tool Improvements - Faster, more efficient hook operations with multi-line selection editing. - Select continuous single blocks by clicking the first block, then **Shift** + click the last block. - For non-continuous blocks, use **Ctrl** (Windows) or **Command** (MacOS) + click each block. - Click and drag mouse left for quick multiple selections. - Modify multiple selected blocks simultaneously by pressing **Shift** or **Ctrl** and double-clicking the last block, then entering the new value and pressing **Return**. ### Benefits - Multi-line selection reduces time spent entering complex code values. - Improved hook editing supports irregular hook adjustments, increasing workflow efficiency.

chunks.content: - Select continuous single blocks by clicking the first block, then **Shift** + click the last block. - For non-continuous blocks, use **Ctrl** (Windows) or **Command** (MacOS) + click each block. - Click and drag mouse left for quick multiple selections. - Modify multiple selected blocks simultaneously by pressing **Shift** or **Ctrl** and double-clicking the last block, then entering the new value and pressing **Return**. ### Benefits - Multi-line selection reduces time spent entering complex code values. - Improved hook editing supports irregular hook adjustments, increasing workflow efficiency. --- ## Checkbox Editor: Virtual Model Layout Improvements This section describes improvements to the **Checkbox Editor** that enhance the layout of virtual models and costumes for size comparison. ### Previous Issue - X-axis distance between virtual models was calculated from the model's center point. - Larger sizes could overlap or appear too close, requiring manual frame adjustments. ### New Calculation Method - X-axis distance is now calculated based on the **border frame and outer edge** of the combined virtual model and costume. - Prevents overlaps even with large sizes (e.g., XXL). - Maintains consistent visible spacing regardless of body shape differences. - Allows comfortable size comparison without manual adjustment. ### How to Use - Open the **Checkbox Editor** via **Production > Checkbox** in the main menu. - Use the panoramic view to display all sizes clearly. - Adjust X-axis distance in the lower right menu and observe spacing changes immediately. ### Benefit - This new standard greatly simplifies checking cross-size layouts, improving accuracy and saving adjustment time. --- ## Consistent Whole Scene View Improvements This section explains updates to the camera view for multiple virtual models (referred to as "horses") aligned in the scene. ### Previous Behavior - Camera lens change caused middle models to appear straight. - Models near edges appeared slanted or curved. - This distortion increased with the number of models. ### Updated Behavior - All models, from smallest to largest, display the **same front cross-section view**. - Models appear lined up straight without distortion. - Easier to compare balance and specific expansions or transformations. - No need to rotate the camera to check small length differences in sleeves or bottoms. - View consistency saves time and improves accuracy in visual inspection. --- ## T-Shape Expansion and Linking Function This section details the **T-shape tool** updates that improve workflow efficiency when working with complex or multi-piece projects. ### Using the T-Shape Expansion Tool - Select the **T-shape tool** from the middle of the 2D window toolbar. - Right-click an existing T-shape and choose **Link Path**. - Click the target T-shape to link. - The guideline appears only when the T-shape tool is activated or a T-shape is selected. - To unlink, right-click the T-shape again and select **Remove Link Path**. ### Purpose and Benefits - Prevents unwanted corrections to linked T-shapes during edits. - Facilitates coordinated corrections and alignment in complex garment areas. - Enhances accuracy and project management when multiple T-shapes are involved.

Together, these features enhance precision, efficiency, and user control in 2D garment design processes.
